equivalents.note: The transcription has an extra ha (pa Da ha for paṭa), as if the translators heard paṭaha, 'drum', the reading behind the rendering rnga'i tshogs pa listed among this entry's forms.
nus ldan, 'possessing power', is an ordinary adjective as well as the rendering of śakti here; the comment repeats it as nus ldan gyi rtsa, 'the channel of the potent one' (cp.11.m2).
gzhom med, 'indestructible, invincible', takes anāhata as 'unassailable' rather than 'unstruck'; the comment expands it to gzhom du med pa'i dbyangs (cp.11.m2).

The Tibetan renders acāre with the verb spyod, 'practises' (zhugs nas spyod, 'having entered, practises'), in step with Munidatta's praviśya pracāreṇa, Tibetan rab tu zhugs nas rab tu spyod pa (cp.11.m2).
rigs gcig means 'of one kind' or 'of one family' and has no word for 'form' (ākāra); the comment has the same, rigs gcig pa (cp.11.m2).

The Tibetan folds kuṇḍala and ābharaṇa into one phrase, rna ba'i rgyan du byas, 'made into ear ornaments', so rgyan also serves for alankara (it also puts the moon before the sun, zla ba nyi ma, against the Bengali rabiśaśī).

The Tibetan line makes two clauses, 'obtains supreme liberation (mchog gi thar thob), holds a pearl necklace', instead of taking liberation as the necklace; the comment keeps the figure, mchog gi thar pa'i mu tig (cp.11.m4).
a ne is usually a paternal aunt, so the Tibetan names a different female relative from the husband's sister.
skud po is a male in-law, a brother-in-law, where śālī is the wife's sister.
The Tibetan reads māa simply as ma, 'mother', not as māyā, whose sgyu ma appears only in Munidatta's paraphrase (cp.11.m5).
The Tibetan kha ni stong pa nyid supports the reading śūnyatā against Shastri's variant śūratā, 'heroism'.
The comment has only mu tig, 'pearl' (mchog gi thar pa'i mu tig gis brgyan, 'adorned with the pearls of supreme liberation'), with no word for the necklace (hāra).

questions: ali is not listed for cp.11.3a, although the Bengali (আলি) and the Tibetan (ཨཱ་ལི A li) both have it there; it is already matched in cp.11.m3, so no separate answer is given.
sakti in cp.11.m2 is not answered separately: the comment uses the same nus ldan (nus ldan gyi rtsa) as the verse line cp.11.1a.
